Borkum Riffgrund 3 · Ørsted / Glennmont

Reported project milestones
2021–22
Glennmont acquired 50%. The announced ~€1.2bn included the stake price and a share of construction payments. Transaction
9M 2024
Ørsted reported a grid-connection delay moving expected commercial operation from Q4 2025 to Q1 2026, with compensation. Interim report
3 Dec 2025
First power generated. Announcement
31 Aug 2026
Commercial operation confirmed by Ørsted; 913 MW capacity. Announcement

Illustrative compensation exercise

Synthetic cash flows per 100 of development cost · not actual investor returns
Case assumptions and evidence boundary
  • Illustration: 3-month opening delay, 6-month revenue ramp, 50 debt, 7% interest, monthly full revenue 2, operating cost 1, maintenance 0.1, pre-opening overhead 0.15, exit at month 60 at 10× EBITDA, 10% discount rate.
  • Assumed compensation: 2.7 in total. Its actual amount and timing are not estimated here. Payment at opening can create multiple cash-flow sign changes; the comparison therefore uses NPV.
  • First power and commercial operation are distinct milestones. The full observed interval cannot be attributed to the grid from these reports alone.
  • The case demonstrates the mechanism. It does not validate the model’s forecast accuracy or reproduce Glennmont’s returns.
How to interpret the results
  • Baseline: the same project inputs with no delay, mitigation or recovery. A positive NPV exceeds the selected discount rate.
  • All development spending and debt draw occur at month 0. Debt interest is paid monthly, principal at exit; debt does not amortize. Equity funds all deficits without a limit.
  • Revenue ramps from opening; operating costs and maintenance start in full at opening. No taxes, inflation, refinancing, fund fees or probabilistic forecasts are included.
  • Recovery uses opening delay attributable to the grid under a stated counterfactual. Eligibility and collection are assumed, not a legal determination.
  • IRR is withheld for nonconventional cash flows or zero terminal enterprise value. Use NPV and inspect the cash-flow view.
  • This is an original project-finance extension motivated by infrastructure dependencies, not a published S³ valuation formula.
